analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata. The workflow removes paid manual dispatch, retains trusted default-branch scanner checkout and pinned actions, and preserves explicit fork opt-in for Bedrock (.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml:64,68-83). It raises the job timeout to 60 minutes, sets a 3000-second scanner deadline, and replaces the 12-call default with workload admission capped by a configurable 500-call ceiling and 16384 output tokens (55,128-140). These changes increase potential paid resource consumption, but the supplied evidence does not establish a budget bypass. Integration must verify workload admission, aggregate spending enforcement, timeout/finalization behavior and rerun rejection in the scanner/state/client implementations; the workflow alone does not enforce the documented rerun prohibition. Conditional clearance still invokes the gate after failures (168-174); its incomplete-result handling needs reconciliation with the changed scanner.
Diagnostics now export completion and call-plan fields (.github/scripts/threat_review/diagnostics.py:80-83); surrounding code avoids raw exception messages and validates revision identifiers. Verify the newly exported snapshot fields remain bounded, content-free internal values at their producers. No observed source disclosure is established here.
The changelog (3-20) and build-guide patch (head 258-267) describe depth routing, workload limits and human handoff, but do not independently prove those controls. No provider encryption, attestation, native inference, cache, fan-helper or release qualification behavior changes in this scope; TB-002/TB-011 and their authorization assumptions are not visibly weakened. The supplied canonical index has no dedicated CI paid-review boundary. Remaining uncertainty concerns the changed CI contracts, not missing unrelated provider implementations.
